entries.title: The first question
entries.quote: Please look at astryx. Should we use that as our css basis for [the family dashboard]?
entries.text: At 7:53 am the owner set the shape: "just like my other apps, I want the core to be in shareable typescript / JavaScript, but ui be native".

entries.title: The spike begins
entries.quote: I want to do a spike for astryx native. Same thing where it's core logic can stay in JavaScript but ui all swift. Generate a rich set of web, Mac and native demo screens. Open source repo [and TestFlight] under me at end.

entries.title: First commit

children.title: What followed
children.description: The work, the design councils, the polish and the eight turning points for quality; times in Pacific time (PT)

entries.title: The bar, in four messages
entries.text: Five requirements: stock and refactored web pixel-perfect; web on Hermes passes the same tests; scenarios that drive native from web and web from native, shipped in the app; a fourth drawing, pure web on its own core; and iOS too.
entries.outcome: From then on "looks right" was never the test; a machine comparison at threshold 0 was.

entries.title: The core and four drawings
entries.text: Native and web on Hermes on one state, web on its own core, and stock Astryx.

entries.title: Why the charts never matched
entries.text: The dashboard agent found that Recharts animates in JavaScript, so waiting for CSS to settle does nothing, and a full-page screenshot resizes the viewport, which restarts the animation. It asked the coordinating session to change the shared harness, which also grew the viewport to the page before each capture and rasterized on one thread.
entries.outcome: The fix went into the shared harness, for every template, not into the dashboard.

entries.title: Ten templates on the core
entries.text: Ten stock templates refactored onto the core, and parity at 1216 of 1216 identical. AstryxKit draws all ten in SwiftUI. First TestFlight builds; the open-source fork.

entries.title: Council: Human Interface Guidelines
entries.text: Five reviewers in parallel with apple-hig-review: the Mac app; iPhone and iPad chrome; data templates; form templates; accessibility. Every finding ruled, then four fix batches (2:27 pm).

entries.title: "Black on blue?"
entries.text: The owner opened the Mac app and asked "black on blue?" and "How did that make it through our design reviewer?" The HIG council had reviewed screens one at a time. The sidebar row was fixed the same hour, with a developer banner that showed in a Release build.
entries.outcome: Native and web reviewed side by side, every screen, every difference ruled: the Mac and iPhone councils.

entries.title: Council: Mac, native against web
entries.text: Five reviewers compared every screen side by side. About 410 differences listed: 45 kept as Mac conventions, each with its HIG citation; about 328 fixed (about 320 native, 8 web or core) by four fix agents (7:21 pm); the rest duplicates of another row or questions ruled.

entries.title: One cause behind many rows
entries.text: A reviewer traced many colour differences to one cause: native painted the page with the body colour (#F1F4F7) where the web uses the surface (#FFFFFF), and Astryx's translucent fills came out darker on grey.
entries.outcome: One fix closed every row citing it.

entries.title: The reviewers checked too
entries.text: Two rulings were wrong: field outlines are Astryx's emphasized border, not its default; field labels are medium weight, not regular.
entries.outcome: Both found by reading the computed styles and Astryx's source instead of trusting screenshots.

entries.title: Council: iPhone, native against web
entries.text: Four reviewers. About 270 differences listed: 99 kept as iOS conventions; about 143 fixed (137 native, 6 web or core) by four fix agents (9:52 pm); the rest duplicates of another row or questions ruled.

entries.title: Polish: layout, text sizes, chart labels
entries.text: Inbox layout moved out of shared state; accessibility text sizes (AX5) for buttons and the kanban toolbar; the dashboard's time labels placed exactly as Recharts places them.

entries.title: Performance, and the issue
entries.text: A hill climb with a frame meter on device and Instruments' hitches and time profiler: 105 fps mean (120 Hz display) on the Mac during scenarios, 57.9 to 59.9 fps on an iPhone 13. The issue draft for the Astryx maintainers.

entries.title: Words and rules into the core
entries.quote: Is there more to push down in the JSX to prevent duplication?
entries.text: Four agents moved every word, layout threshold and search into the core: the JSX holds no English and no breakpoint of its own.
entries.outcome: Moving the kanban card's words fixed four parity differences on the way.

entries.title: Saved data without breaking parity
entries.text: Three agents moved the templates onto saved data. Stock mode (?stock=1) keeps the harness comparing like with like.
entries.outcome: It caught that a moved kanban card must keep stock's "Edited 2h ago" and its place in board order.

entries.title: Saved work and sign-in
entries.text: One mutation definition run by the core, Zero's client and the server. Zero in Hermes, with SQLite on the device. Optional sign-in through Cloudflare Access. Its own AWS account and Terraform repository.

entries.title: Polish: sign-in lasts until sign-out
entries.text: Rotating refresh tokens; reusing a replaced one after two minutes ends the session.

entries.title: A font, not the code
entries.text: After the build container was rebuilt, the chat replay failed by 71,955 pixels on every step, while stock and ours still matched each other.
entries.outcome: The cause was a missing font (DejaVu Sans Mono), not the code.

children.title: Found without being asked
children.description: What the most insightful agents found

items.label: Dashboard refactor
items.value: Recharts animates in JavaScript, and a full-page screenshot restarts it: the two causes behind the charts' differences.

items.label: Compare reviewer, templates B
items.value: The single page-colour cause behind many rows.

items.label: Performance hill climb
items.value: On the Mac every long frame gap (290 to 450 ms) followed a sheet opening or closing, because AppKit animates sheets on the main thread; on iPhone, sheets did not stop frames.

items.label: Sync builder
items.value: Its end-to-end test found a lock key with a NUL byte, which Postgres text cannot hold; it replaced read-then-write with one upsert, so two devices creating the same row never collide.

items.label: Settings and demo screens
items.value: After a relaunch, new record ids restarted at 1 and could overwrite saved rows; minting now skips ids already saved, with a test.

items.label: Checkout
items.value: Order totals in integer cents, checked against the dollar figures the page shows for 270 cart combinations.

items.label: Apple sync
items.value: Zero needed three things Hermes lacks (Symbol.asyncIterator, TextDecoder, a URL that keeps Zero's paths); it wrote a UTF-8 decoder to the standard and fuzzed it against Node's: 30,000 cases, no mismatches.

items.label: Infrastructure
items.value: The account's apply role would have exceeded an IAM policy size limit as a new policy; it added statements to the existing one, as the newest account had.
